back: The part of the day before noon. In the morning, I drink coffee.
To start sleeping at night. I go to bed at eleven.
To wash your body with water in a shower. I shower before work.
To make food with heat. I cook dinner on Sundays.
To make a place tidy and free of dirt. I clean the flat on Saturdays.
To buy food and things in shops. We go shopping every week.
The work you do to earn money. My job is in sales.
To begin your working day. I start work at nine.
A time when people come together to talk about work. We have a meeting at ten.
To write and send a message electronically. I send emails all morning.
A document that gives information about work. I write a report every Friday.
A goal you aim to reach. We reached our sales target.
A trip by plane. The flight was delayed.
A large bag for clothes on a trip. My suitcase is heavy.
A place to stay when you travel. We stayed in a small hotel.
A drawing of a place that shows the roads. Can you check the map?
To arrive after the train has left. I missed the train.
To not know where you are. We got lost in the old town.
To have a body temperature that is too high. She has a fever.
To do physical activity to stay fit. I exercise three times a week.
A substance you take when you are ill. Take this medicine twice a day.
To have a good night of sleep. I didn't sleep well last night.
The food you eat each day, which keeps you well. I try to eat a healthy diet.
To visit a doctor for advice or treatment. You should see a doctor.
To use a bank card to pay. Can I pay by card?
How big or small clothes are. What size do you need?
A paper that shows what you bought and paid. Keep the receipt for returns.
To take a product back to the shop. I want to return this shirt.
A lower price than normal. There is a ten percent discount.
A product bought for much less than its usual price. This jacket was a real bargain.
1:30. It is half past one.
5:45. I leave at quarter to six.
The day, month, and year. Today is the fifth of May.
The number 1,000. It costs two thousand pounds.
A period of close to sixty minutes. We talked for about an hour.
A part of a whole, out of one hundred. Sales rose by twelve percent.
Routines and facts. Formula: I / you / we / they + verb; he / she / it + verb + s. Example: She works in a bank.
Finished actions at a finished time. Formula: verb + ed, or an irregular form. Example: I worked yesterday.
Plans and intentions. Formula: am / is / are + going to + verb. Example: I am going to study tonight.
Actions happening now or around now. Formula: am / is / are + verb-ing. Example: I am working from home this week.
Experience or a link from the past to now. Formula: have / has + past participle. Example: I have visited Spain twice.
Real future possibilities. Formula: If + present simple, will + verb. Example: If it rains, I will stay home.
Imagined present situations. Formula: If + past simple, would + verb. Example: If I had more time, I would travel.
Imagined past situations. Formula: If + past perfect, would have + past participle. Example: If I had studied, I would have passed.
Adding information about a person or thing. Formula: noun + who / which / that + clause. Example: The man who called is my manager.
Opinion, size, age, colour, then noun. Example: a beautiful big red car.
When the action matters more than the doer. Formula: object + is / was + past participle. Example: The report was written by the team.
Yes or no questions in the present. Formula: Do / Does + subject + verb? Example: Do you like coffee?
